rendered: The authors did not choose room temperature as the separation condition. Room-temperature filtration was a control that showed what goes wrong when the process cools. Cyrene dissolves PVDF only when hot, and PVDF comes back out of solution as the mixture cools. The authors state that PVDF would precipitate out if the temperature was low[1]. At room temperature the PVDF/Cyrene mixture gels: started to precipitate out and gelation occurred[2]. They therefore kept the separation above the dissolution temperature: the separation process should be kept above that[3]. In the FTIR comparison, the powder filtered at room temperature still showed PVDF, meaning the binder had reprecipitated onto the cathode particles on cooling: the reprecipitation of PVDF along with the cathode particles after[4]. The hot-filtered powder lacked that band: The absence of the typical band[5]. Hot filtration was therefore the method adopted for separating the foils and black mass.
